prompt_text: Who is a reliable contractor in Joplin MO for a home remodel or repair project?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — I don’t want to give names I can’t verify from current reviews, but I can quickly find and vet reliable Joplin contractors for you if you’d like. First, a few quick questions that will let me give the best recommendations:

- What kind of work is it (full remodel, kitchen, bathroom, roof, siding, electrical, plumbing, general repairs)?  
- What’s your ZIP code or neighborhood in Joplin?  
- Rough budget and timeframe?  
- Do you prefer contractors who handle permits and subs, or do you want someone to do a single trade?

If you want to search on your own now, here are reliable ways to find and vet contractors in Joplin, MO:

Where to look
- Google and Google Maps: read recent reviews and look at photos.  
- Angi (formerly Angie’s List), HomeAdvisor, Houzz: good for remodel pros and project photos.  
- Better Business Bureau (BBB) for complaints and ratings.  
- Yelp and Facebook community groups (Joplin area groups or Nextdoor) for word-of-mouth referrals.  
- Local building department (City of Joplin Building Division) to confirm permit history and any code issues.  
- Ask neighbors/homeowners who have done similar projects for referrals.

How to vet contractors
- Verify trade licensing where applicable (electrical and plumbing often require state/local licenses). For other trades check business registration and insurance.  
- Confirm current General Liability insurance and workers’ compensation (ask for certificates).  
- Ask for at least 3 recent local references and follow up with them.  
- Get 3 written bids with the same scope so you can compare apples-to-apples.  
- Make sure the contractor will obtain required permits; ask who handles inspections.  
- Request a written contract that includes scope, materials, payment schedule, start/finish dates, cleanup, and warranty.  
- Check online reviews and BBB complaints; pay special attention to how the contractor responds to problems.

Questions to ask a potential contractor
- Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide proof?  
- Can you give three local references from similar projects? May I see photos?  
- Who will be on site and who is your point of contact? Do you use subcontractors?  
- What is your estimated timeline and payment schedule?  
- How do you handle change orders and unexpected issues?  
- What warranties do you offer on labor and materials?

Warning signs / red flags
- High-pressure tactics or asking for large upfront cash payments.  
- Vague or no written contract.  
- No proof of insurance or license where required.  
- Poor or no local references and many unresolved complaints.  
- Unwillingness to obtain permits.

If you want, I can:
- Search for 3–5 well-rated Joplin contractors for your specific project and summarize their credentials, reviews, and how they compare; or  
- Draft a short email/script you can use to request bids and ask the right questions.

Tell me which option you prefer and give the project details/ZIP code and I’ll start.
